- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)
- code-simplifier:code-simplifier: Simplifies and refines code for clarity, consistency, and maintainability while preserving all functionality. Focuses on recently modified code unless instructed otherwise. (Tools: All tools)
- coderabbit:code-reviewer: Specialized CodeRabbit code review agent that performs thorough analysis of code changes (Tools: All tools)
- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- feature-factory:spec-challenger: Adversarial reviewer for a feature spec / design document. Use after a spec is drafted (Stage 2 of the feature-factory pipeline) to attack it before any code is written - finding gaps, ambiguities, unstated assumptions, edge cases, and weak design decisions. Returns a severity-tagged critique and an overall verdict. This is the automated replacement for "ask another Opus to challenge the spec". (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob)
- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)
- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

When you launch multiple agents for independent work, send them in a single message with multiple tool uses so they run concurrently.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## claude.ai Hugging Face
Prefer these Hugging Face tools over web search for live Hub data; start with hf_fs.
Hugging Face tools are being used by authenticated user 'smaschek'

## claude.ai Linear
When passing string values to tools, send the content directly without escape sequences. For example, use real newlines in markdown content rather than literal backslash-n (\n) characters.

Tools accept human-readable references, so you rarely need to look up IDs first: issue identifiers such as LIN-123, project identifiers such as P-ENG-12, team names or keys, user names or emails, and "me" for the authenticated user. Only call list_teams, list_users, or similar tools when a reference is ambiguous or unknown.

Use list_issues for structured queries, such as the issues assigned to "me" in a team, status, label, project, or cycle, and its query parameter for keyword search. Results are paginated: when hasNextPage is true, pass the returned cursor to fetch the next page rather than assuming the first page is complete.

Statuses and labels belong to teams and differ between them. When you are not sure which values a team supports, call list_issue_statuses or list_issue_labels for that team before filtering or setting them.

get_issue does not include the issue's discussion. Call list_comments with the issue ID to read comments, including inline comments on the description.

Issue descriptions, comments, and documents often embed screenshots and other uploads as markdown images. Pass that markdown to extract_images to view them. Read issue attachments with get_attachment; files uploaded in comments are returned in the attachments field of list_comments. Linear upload URLs are signed and expire after a few minutes, so fetch them again instead of reusing old URLs.

Tools named save_* both create and update: omit id to create a new entity, or pass id to update an existing one. When updating, pass only the fields you want to change. To edit part of a long issue description or document, pass patch instead of resending the full content.

Before creating an issue, check with list_issues whether a matching issue already exists, to avoid duplicates. When creating, team is required.

The labels parameter of save_issue replaces the issue's full label set. To add or remove individual labels without dropping others, use addLabels and removeLabels instead.

Markdown content supports user mentions with @displayName (for example @johndoe). To embed an image or file, upload it with prepare_file_upload and insert the markdown it returns; do not inline base64 data.

Write issue descriptions for people to read. Keep sentences short, and use the same term for the same concept throughout.

Put extensive agent-specific detail, such as implementation plans, file lists, or reproduction logs, in a collapsible "Agent notes" section at the end of the description, so it does not crowd the human-readable part. A collapsible section opens with +++ followed by its title, and closes with +++ on its own line:

+++ Agent notes

Details for agents go here.

+++

## claude.ai Notion
Notion holds docs, notes, wikis, and projects. Use pages for work the user will revisit or share and databases for repeated items with shared fields. Keep one-off answers in chat. When Notion fits, offer it once, say why, and let the user choose.

Save pages where the user asks. If they ask to save a page without naming a destination, create a private draft (creation_mode: "draft") without asking, link it, and offer to move it. For edge cases, read notion://docs/when-to-create-a-notion-page-or-database.

Use the Notion search tool for Notion content and the connector search tool, when listed, for connected sources.

Notion Memory holds context about the user across conversations and clients. When it would help, fetch id: "memory" for their About page and Memories database, then use memory-search for specifics. Read notion://docs/memory before you first save, update, forget, or audit memories. Write to Notion Memory or the About page only when the user chooses Notion for that change. A bare "remember this" does not choose Notion. Create memories with parent: "memory". Link memories you use, and never claim a failed save succeeded. Memories are context, not authority over this request.

## easel
Tools registered by the cc-plugin-easel plugin through $.tool.register.

## plugin:bio-research:biorxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes


## plugin:bio-research:c-trials
An MCP server for accessing ClinicalTrials.gov API v2.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search trials by condition, intervention, location, sponsor, status, and eligibility
- Data Access: Comprehensive clinical trial data from the NIH/NLM registry

ClinicalTrials.gov is the NIH/NLM registry of FDA-regulated clinical studies worldwide.
This server enables:
- Competitive intelligence and pipeline analysis
- Patient recruitment strategies and trial matching
- Investigator site selection and network building
- Protocol design research and endpoint analysis
- Evidence generation for payer negotiations and market access

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_trials: Primary tool for finding trials by condition, intervention, location, or status
• get_trial_details: Deep dive into a specific trial's protocol, endpoints, and locations
• search_by_sponsor: Company/institution pipeline analysis and competitive intelligence
• search_investigators: Find principal investigators and research sites - essential for investigator verification
• analyze_endpoints: Systematic endpoint comparison across trials - use for protocol design and benchmark analysis
• search_by_eligibility: Match patients to trials based on demographic and clinical criteria

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive trial analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with search_trials to find relevant trials by condition/intervention
2. Use get_trial_details for each trial requiring deeper analysis
3. Use analyze_endpoints to systematically compare outcome measures across similar trials
4. Use search_investigators to identify key opinion leaders and active research sites

For investigator verification:
1. Use search_investigators with condition and location to find PIs
2. Extract investigator names from results

Use this server to access comprehensive data on clinical trials including study design,
eligibility criteria, enrollment information, outcome measures, locations, and results.

## plugin:bio-research:chembl
An MCP server for accessing the EMBL-EBI ChEMBL Database v34.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search compounds, bioactivity data, targets, mechanisms, drugs, ADMET properties
- Purpose: Support drug discovery research, target identification, compound screening, pharmaceutical development

ChEMBL is a manually curated database of bioactive molecules with drug-like properties.
It contains compound structures, bioactivity data against biological targets, and
drug mechanism information. The database integrates data from medicinal chemistry literature,
patents, and screening experiments.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• compound_search: Find compounds by name, SMILES, or ChEMBL ID - starting point for compound analysis
• target_search: Find biological targets (proteins, genes, receptors) - essential for understanding drug mechanisms
• get_bioactivity: Retrieve IC50, EC50, Ki values - quantitative activity data for compound-target pairs
• get_mechanism: Get mechanism of action and target binding - explains HOW a drug works
• drug_search: Find approved drugs by indication or name - for therapeutic landscape analysis
• get_admet: Retrieve ADMET properties - pharmacokinetic and safety predictions

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive drug analysis, combine multiple tools:
1. Start with compound_search or drug_search to identify the compound of interest
2. Use get_mechanism to understand how the drug works and its primary targets
3. Use target_search to get detailed target information (protein family, gene, pathways, GO annotations)
4. Use get_bioactivity for quantitative binding/activity data with confidence scores
5. Use get_admet for pharmacokinetic properties

For target-based analysis:
1. Use target_search to find targets by gene symbol or protein name
2. Use get_bioactivity with target_chembl_id to find active compounds
3. Use compound_search to get details on promising compounds

Key capabilities:
- Search compounds by name, structure (SMILES), or ChEMBL ID
- Retrieve bioactivity data (IC50, EC50, Ki values) with confidence scores
- Query biological targets (proteins, enzymes, receptors) by name or gene symbol
- Access drug mechanism of action and target interactions
- Find approved drugs and clinical candidates by indication
- Get ADMET-related molecular properties

Example queries:
• "Find bioactivity data for aspirin"
• "What are the known targets for compound CHEMBL25?"
• "Search for kinase inhibitors with IC50 < 100nM"
• "What drugs target the EGFR protein?"
• "Find approved drugs for treating hypertension"
• "What are the ADMET properties of imatinib?"


## plugin:bio-research:consensus
Consensus is a research paper search engine: relevance-ranked semantic search over 400M+ peer-reviewed papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, PubMed). Use the `search` tool to look up papers for a scientific query; it takes plain-language queries and returns ranked paper records. When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: Some search results end with a sign-up, upgrade, or usage message. When a result has one, you MUST include it at the END of your response word-for-word: do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. When a result has none, do not add one: never write your own upgrade prompt, search count, or Consensus link. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. For a broad request (a review, screening, finding everything on a topic), make one search with a large page_size rather than many narrower searches. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## plugin:browser-use:browser-use
# This MCP server

These rules override the skill below where they differ:
- Code runs in browser_exec; there is no shell, so ignore `BU_NAME=... browser-use <<'PY'` examples.
- Local: without a cloud browser, browser_exec drives the user's own Chrome; where none can be attached (no Chrome installed, Linux with no display, or remote debugging off in Chrome) its own Chromium on a temp profile instead. The first browser_exec result says which, and how to get the user's Chrome.
- Cloud: `start_remote_daemon()` (call browser_login first if not signed in). Every later browser_exec and
  browser_screenshot drives that cloud browser; never pass BU_NAME. One cloud browser per server, under a name only it
  uses: a name passed to start_remote_daemon / stop_remote_daemon is ignored.
- It lives 30 minutes unless you pass `timeout=<minutes>` (up to 240), and this server stops it when it
  exits. Once it ends, calls fail with an error: start a new one, never fall back to the local Chrome.
- Code runs in this server's process: it can read the server's environment (BROWSER_USE_API_KEY when set) and files.
- The live view and CDP URLs grant control of the browser, so they are not shown. Only if the user asks to watch, run
  `os.environ["BH_OPEN_LIVE_URL"] = "1"` before start_remote_daemon: the live view then opens in their browser, and
  both are returned.

# Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, run `browser-use --doctor` and follow its output and the error message.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background; call `activate_tab(target)` only when the user explicitly asks
  or a page demonstrably pauses rendering while hidden.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timed-out `scroll(...)` on an attached background tab is evide… [truncated]

While auto mode is active:

You can do much of your work through the Bash tool when it is the simpler route: read files with cat, head, or sed -n, search with grep and find, and make small, mechanical file changes with sed, heredocs, or short scripts instead of the dedicated Read, Edit, or Write tools. The choice is yours: prefer Edit or Write when a shell edit would be fragile, such as exact or multi-line replacements, or sed/awk flags that differ between GNU and BSD/macOS.

1075	+> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

1077	+**Goal:** The Gemini request translator names each `functionResponse` from the call it closes (FIFO), and never sends two adjacent contents with the same role.
1078	+
1079	+**Architecture:** `items_to_contents` keeps one pass in item order. The pass produces `(role, parts)` entries; a final fold drops empty entries and merges adjacent entries with the same role.

1272	+# SMA-820: Gemini translator merges same-role contents and names each tool result from its own call
1273	+
1274	+Linear: [SMA-820](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-820/gemini-translator-sends-two-adjacent-user-contents-after-a-tool-result).
1275	+Size: a small change in the Gemini translator. Files: `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/translate/request.rs`,
1276	+`.../src/translate/mod.rs` (inline asserts in `snap_parallel_same_name_tool_calls`), the snapshots in
1277	+`.../src/translate/snapshots/`, and `.../tests/live.rs`.
1278	+
1279	+## Intent
1280	+
1281	+`items_to_contents` makes one Gemini content for each core `Item`. Two defects follow.
1282	+
1283	+1. **Adjacent same-role contents.** A tool result becomes a `role: user` content with a
1284	+   `functionResponse` part. When a user message comes directly after it, the request has two
1285	+   adjacent `role: user` contents. Known sources of this shape:
1286	+   - a turn-boundary checkpoint that returns `Inject(..)` after a tool turn (PR #346);
1287	+   - a resumed run after a deferred tool call;
1288	+   - a synthetic cancel result followed by the input of the next run;
1289	+   - the handoff transcript note after a user message, when the transfer turn had no text
1290	+     (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:770-789`);
1291	+   - the `CompactingSession` prompt after a snapshot that ends in a tool result.
1292	+   Parallel calls also give adjacent `model` contents (one per `ToolCall`) and adjacent `user`
1293	+   contents (one per result).
1294	+2. **Wrong name on a repeated call id.** The translator resolves a `functionResponse` name from one
1295	+   global `call_id -> name` map, and the last call wins. `stream.rs` makes the fallback ids
1296	+   `fc_{n}` per stream, so two turns can both have a call `fc_0`. Then an earlier result gets the
1297	+   name of a later call (turn 1 `search`/`fc_0`, turn 2 `pay`/`fc_0` → the `search` result is sent
1298	+   as `pay`).
1299	+
1300	+## Goals
1301	+
1302	+- The translator never sends two adjacent contents with the same role. It merges them into one
1303	+  content and keeps the order of the parts.
1304	+- The rule applies to every item, so replayed session items are also covered.
1305	+- Each `functionResponse` gets the name of the call that it closes, by the core pairing rule
1306	+  (below), within the limits in "Known limits".
1307	+
1308	+## Non-goals
1309	+
1310	+- Gemini thought signatures and `ContentPart::Reasoning` translation (still deferred, D3).
1311	+- Changes to the fallback id scheme in `stream.rs`. A unique fallback id would remove the collision
1312	+  for new histories, but stored sessions already hold repeated `fc_0` ids, so the translator must
1313	+  pair by order anyway. A follow-up Linear issue can track the id scheme.
1314	+- Changes to other providers.
1315	+
1316	+## Approaches
1317	+
1318	+1. **Merge after translation (picked).** Translate each item to `(role, parts)` as today, then fold
1319	+   adjacent entries with the same role into one content. One small post-pass covers every source
1320	+   of adjacency with one rule.
1321	+2. **Merge at each push site.** Each branch checks the last content and appends to it. This repeats
1322	+   the same check in five branches, and a new branch can forget it.
1323	+3. **Reorder items in core before the provider sees them.** Rejected: the problem is a Gemini wire
1324	+   rule, and other providers accept the core order as it is.
1325	+
1326	+Sven approved approach 1 on 2026-11-20, and approved this spec at GATE 1 on 2026-11-20.
1327	+
1328	+## Design
1329	+
1330	+### Merge
1331	+
1332	+- Build a `Vec<(role, Vec<Value>)>` in item order, then fold it: when the role of an entry equals
1333	+  the role of the last merged entry, append its parts; else start a new content.
1334	+- **Exception, the tool-result boundary** (added 2026-11-20 after the live run, Sven's decision):
1335	+  a `user` entry whose first part is not a `functionResponse` does not merge into a `user` content
1336	+  whose last part is a `functionResponse`. It starts a new `user` content. So a user text after a
1337	+  tool result stays a separate content, as on `main`.
1338	+  - Reason: Gemini 3 checks thought signatures only in the current turn, and the current turn
1339	+    starts at the last `user` content that is not a tool result. With the merge, `user[fr, text]`
1340	+    keeps the call in the current turn, and the translator sends no signature (SMA-827): HTTP 400
1341	+    (probe shape 3 with no signature; the first live run of this branch failed 3 of 3 this way).
1342	+    The split shape gets HTTP 200 with and without a signature (probe shape 2).
1343	+  - Consequence: the SMA-804 `Inject` shape stays two adjacent `user` contents. The probe shows
1344	+    that Gemini accepts it. Parallel results, adjacent user texts, and all `model` contents still
1345	+    merge. Review this exception when SMA-827 lands.
1346	+- An entry with no parts is dropped before the fold. Today only an empty `user` content is
1347	+  dropped. An assistant message with only `Reasoning` parts gives a `model` content with
1348	+  `"parts": []`.
1349	+- An empty `ContentPart::Text` (`text == ""`) in a user or assistant message is dropped (SMA-804
1350	+  spec §5.3 asks every translator to do this; SMA-819 did it for Anthropic). Without this, the
1351	+  merge puts `{"text": ""}` into the content with the `functionResponse`.
1352	+- `Item::System` stays in `systemInstruction` and does not take part in the merge. Items that the
1353	+  translator skips, and `System` items, do not break adjacency.
1354	+- Intended consequences:
1355	+  - Parallel calls: N adjacent `ToolCall` items become one `model` content with N `functionCall`
1356	+    parts, and N results become one `user` content with N `functionResponse` parts.
1357	+  - An assistant text followed by its `ToolCall` becomes one `model` content (text part, then
1358	+    `functionCall` part).
1359	+  - Two adjacent user texts become two `text` parts in one content. They are not joined.
1360	+- The order of parallel `functionCall` parts is the core item order. `build_items` in core emits
1361	+  calls in `BTreeMap<call_id, _>` order (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:514,530`), so
1362	+  `fc_10` comes before `fc_2`. This spec does not change that. Note for D3: Gemini 3 puts the
1363	+  thought signature on the first `functionCall` part.
1364	+- The empty-conversation error stays: if no content remains after the fold, return the error.
1365	+
1366	+### Name resolution (core pairing rule, FIFO)
1367	+
1368	+- One pass in item order. The pass keeps a list of open calls (call id, name), in order. The
1369	+  translator must not store names by call id in a pre-pass, because that brings the defect back.
1370	+  The open-call state goes `&mut` into `user_parts`, or the pass stores names by occurrence.
1371	+  - A `ToolCall` item, or a `ContentPart::ToolUse` in an `AssistantMessage`, adds an open call.
1372	+  - A result (`Item::ToolResult`, or `ContentPart::ToolResult` in a `UserMessage`) closes the
1373	+    **earliest** open call with its id and takes that name.
1374	+- This is the rule that core uses: `resume_exec::paired_result` (`resume_exec.rs:200-220`, "each
1375	+  result closes the earliest open call with its call id", "as in the session recorder") and
1376	+  `deferral::agent_view` (`deferral.rs:585-620`). `run_tools_concurrent` returns one outcome per
1377	+  call in call order (`agent.rs:748`). With FIFO, two calls in one round that share `fc_0` get the
1378	+  correct names. The cross-turn `search`/`pay` case also works.
1379	+  - **This changes the ticket text.** The ticket says "the most recent earlier call with the same
1380	+    id that has no result yet" (LIFO). LIFO gives both names wrong for two same-id calls in one
1381	+    round, where `main` gives one of two. Sven chose FIFO at GATE 1 on 2026-11-20.
1382	+- A result that closes no open call, but that has an earlier call with its id (a second result for
1383	+  one call), is **dropped** with a `tracing::warn!` (target `paigasus::gemini::translate`). This
1384	+  matches `agent_view`, which drops a result that closes no open call. It also prevents a merged
1385	+  `user` content with more `functionResponse` parts than its `functionCall` parts. (This replaces
1386	+  the earlier call "use the most recent earlier call", which could send two responses for one
1387	+  call.)
1388	+- A result whose id has no earlier call returns an error:
1389	+  - if a later item has a call with that id: a new message, `tool result for call_id {id} comes
1390	+    before its call`;
1391	+  - else the existing `tool result references unknown call_id {id}`.
1392	+- Behavior change: a result before its call now gives an error. Today the global map accepts it.
1393	+  No core producer makes this order: `close_open_transfers` inserts at `at + 1`
1394	+  (`resume_exec.rs:194`), the resume block follows the calls of the earlier run, and the legacy
1395	+  repair moves results after their calls. A stored session in this order now fails at `invoke`
1396	+  instead of being sent. The commit message names this error so that the CHANGELOG shows it.
1397	+
1398	+### Invariant and known limits
1399	+
1400	+The merge depends on one invariant: the next `user` content answers each `functionCall` of a
1401	+`model` content. Two real core histories do not hold it:
1402	+
1403	+1. **Open deferred calls.** `RunDeferred` leaves calls with no result. `CompactingSession` sends
1404	+   `snapshot + prompt` to its model (`compacting_session.rs:200-211`). With a Gemini summarizer
1405	+   this gives, for example, `model[fc c1, fc c2], user[fr c1, text]`. Probe shape 14 shows what
1406	+   Gemini does with it. This spec does not add synthetic results; if shape 14 fails, a follow-up
1407	+   issue covers it.
1408	+2. **Replay of a `ParallelAgent` session.** Sibling events interleave through `select_all`
1409	+   (`workflow.rs:377`), and sibling Gemini agents all start at `fc_0`. The merge can put two
1410	+   `functionCall` parts with the same id into one content. No order rule can name those results
1411	+   correctly. This spec does not fix it.
1412	+
1413	+## Tests
1414	+
1415	+Unit tests in `request.rs` assert the full `contents` array, as
1416	+`tool_result_then_user_message_request_shape` does:
1417	+
1418	+- `tool_result_then_user_message_request_shape` (and its doc comment): the assistant text and
1419	+  the call merge into one `model` content; the `functionResponse` content and the user text stay
1420	+  two `user` contents (the tool-result boundary). The ticket asked for one merged `user` content;
1421	+  Sven changed that on 2026-11-20 after the live run.
1422	+- The tool-result boundary: a user text after results stays separate; a result after a result
1423	+  still merges; a user text after a user text still merges.
1424	+- More than two adjacent contents with the same role merge into one, in order (a result, then two
1425	+  user messages).
1426	+- Two calls in different turns that share `fc_0` (`search`, then `pay`): correct name on each
1427	+  `functionResponse`.
1428	+- Two calls in one round that share `fc_0` (`search`, then `pay`), as two `ToolCall` items and as
1429	+  two `ToolUse` parts in one `AssistantMessage`: the first result is `search`, the second `pay`.
1430	+- Results in a different order than the calls (distinct ids): each gets its own name.
1431	+- A second result for one call is dropped.
1432	+- A result before its call gives the new error.
1433	+- A nested `ContentPart::ToolResult` mixed with `Text` in a `UserMessage`, directly after an
1434	+  `Item::ToolResult`: one merged `user` content with correct names.
1435	+- An `Item::System` between two user messages: one merged `user` content.
1436	+- A reasoning-only assistant message is dropped and its neighbours merge.
1437	+- An empty `Text` part is dropped.
1438	+
1439	+Snapshots: update `snap_parallel_same_name_tool_calls` and its inline asserts in `mod.rs`, and any
1440	+other snapshot that the merge changes. Review each snapshot diff by hand.
1441	+
1442	+Live test (mandatory, `#[ignore]` in `tests/live.rs`, needs `GEMINI_API_KEY`): call
1443	+`GeminiModel::invoke` with `search` and `pay` declared, for three histories: the SMA-804 shape
1444	+(result then user text), one parallel round, and a cross-turn `fc_0` collision. Assert no `Err`
1445	+event and a `Finish` event. This is the "after" check through the real translator.
1446	+
1447	+## Live check (acceptance criterion)
1448	+
1449	+The probe `probe.sh` sends hand-made request bodies to `gemini-2.5-flash` through the REST API
1450	+(`generateContent`), with `search` and `pay` declared. It prints the HTTP status, the finish reason
1451	+and a short part summary. It never prints request headers. The probe source goes into the commit
1452	+body. Shapes:
1453	+
1454	+1. baseline: `user, model[fc], user[fr]`
1455	+2. SMA-804 today: `..., user[fr], user[text]`
1456	+3. SMA-804 merged: `..., user[fr, text]`
1457	+4. three adjacent `user` contents
1458	+5. parallel today: `model[fc0], model[fc1], user[fr0], user[fr1]`
1459	+6. parallel merged: `model[fc0, fc1], user[fr0, fr1]`
1460	+7. `functionResponse` name differs from its `functionCall` name
1461	+8. repeated `fc_0` across turns, correct names
1462	+9. repeated `fc_0` across turns, today's wrong name
1463	+10. `model[text, fc]`
1464	+11. parallel merged, responses in a different order than the calls
1465	+12. `user[fr, {"text": ""}]`
1466	+13. two `functionResponse` parts for one call
1467	+14. parallel merged, one call has no response, then text
1468	+
1469	+Pass rule for a target shape (3, 6, 8, 10, 11): HTTP 200, `finishReason: STOP`, and an answer that
1470	+uses the tool result.
1471	+
1472	+Order: run the probe **before** any code. If Gemini rejects shape 3 or 6, stop and bring it back to
1473	+Sven before implementation (fallback: keep the merge for `model` contents only, or put the text in a
1474	+separate content after a synthetic `model` turn; Sven decides).
1475	+
1476	+### Results before the fix (2026-11-20, Developer API, hand-made bodies)
1477	+
1478	+`gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`: HTTP 404 on every shape, "no longer available to
1479	+new users". The probe therefore ran on `gemini-3.8-flash`.
1480	+
1481	+`gemini-3.8-flash` with no `thoughtSignature`: HTTP 400 "Function call is missing a
1482	+thought_signature in functionCall parts" on every shape in which the call is in the current turn
1483	+(1, 3, 5-14). Shapes 2 and 4 returned HTTP 200 / `STOP`, because the trailing user text moves the
1484	+call into an earlier turn, and Gemini checks signatures only in the current turn.
1485	+
1486	+`gemini-3.8-flash` with the documented dummy signature `skip_thought_signature_validator` on each
1487	+`functionCall` part:
1488	+
1489	+| Shape | Result |
1490	+|---|---|
1491	+| 1 baseline | 200 STOP, uses the result |
1492	+| 2 SMA-804 today (two adjacent `user`) | 200 STOP, uses the result |
1493	+| 3 SMA-804 merged | 200 STOP, uses the result |
1494	+| 4 three adjacent `user` | 200 STOP |
1495	+| 5 parallel today | 200 STOP |
1496	+| 6 parallel merged | 200 STOP |
1497	+| 7 response name differs from call name | **400 "Request contains an invalid argument."** |
1498	+| 8 repeated `fc_0`, correct names | 200 STOP |
1499	+| 9 repeated `fc_0`, today's wrong name | **400 "Request contains an invalid argument."** |
1500	+| 10 `model[text, fc]` | 200 STOP |
1501	+| 11 merged, responses reordered | 200 STOP |
1502	+| 12 `user[fr, {"text": ""}]` | 200 STOP |
1503	+| 13 two responses for one call | 200 STOP |
1504	+| 14 merged, one call with no response | 200 STOP, the model calls `search` again |
1505	+
1506	+What this means:
1507	+
1508	+- Defect 1 (adjacent same-role contents) causes no failure on `gemini-3.8-flash`. With a signature,
1509	+  both the split and the merged shapes are accepted. Without a signature, only the split shape is
1510	+  accepted (shapes 2 vs 3). So the merge keeps the tool-result boundary (see "Merge").
1511	+- Defect 2 (wrong name) is a **hard failure**: HTTP 400 on the next model call. Part 2 is the fix
1512	+  that matters for users.
1513	+- Gemini accepts a second response for one call (13). The translator still drops it, to match core.
1514	+- Shape 14 (an open call with no response) is accepted. Known limit 1 causes no API error.
1515	+
1516	+### Out of scope, found by the probe
1517	+
1518	+The Gemini provider does not read or send `thoughtSignature` (no match in `crates/`). With a
1519	+current Gemini model, every request in which the current turn holds a `functionCall` gets HTTP 400.
1520	+So tool loops on Gemini 3.x fail at the second model call. SMA-827 tracks this. The model ids in
1521	+the crate docs and in `tests/live.rs` (`gemini-2.5-flash`) are not available to new users; SMA-565
1522	+tracks them. This PR changes only the `tests/live.rs` default (below); the other occurrences stay
1523	+in SMA-565.
1524	+
1525	+### After the fix
1526	+
1527	+The live test in `tests/live.rs` runs through the real translator. Because the translator sends no
1528	+thought signatures, each history in the test ends with a user text after the last tool result. With
1529	+the tool-result boundary, that text is a separate `user` content, so no call is in the current turn.
1530	+(The first version of this section assumed this without the boundary. The first live run proved it
1531	+wrong: 3 of 3 tests got HTTP 400 for a missing thought signature.) Shape 9 shows that Gemini checks names in earlier turns too, so the
1532	+cross-turn `fc_0` history still tests the name fix. The test model defaults to `gemini-3.8-flash`
1533	+(override with `GEMINI_MODEL_ID`); the default of the existing `dev_model()` changes from
1534	+`gemini-2.5-flash` to `gemini-3.8-flash`, because the old default returns 404 for new users.
1535	+

+# SMA-820 Gemini same-role merge and FIFO tool-result naming Implementation Plan
+
+> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.
+
+**Goal:** The Gemini request translator names each `functionResponse` from the call it closes (FIFO), and never sends two adjacent contents with the same role.
+
+**Architecture:** `items_to_contents` keeps one pass in item order. An `OpenCalls` value replaces the global `call_id -> name` map: calls open entries, results close the earliest open entry with their id. The pass produces `(role, parts)` entries; a final fold drops empty entries and merges adjacent entries with the same role.
+
+**Tech Stack:** Rust, `serde_json`, `insta` snapshots, `tracing`, `tokio` (live tests).

+**Spec:** `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-820-gemini-merge-same-role-contents-design.md`

+# SMA-820: Gemini translator merges same-role contents and names each tool result from its own call
+
+Linear: [SMA-820](https://linear.app/smaschek/issue/SMA-820/gemini-translator-sends-two-adjacent-user-contents-after-a-tool-result).
+Size: a small change in the Gemini translator. Files: `crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/translate/request.rs`,
+`.../src/translate/mod.rs` (inline asserts in `snap_parallel_same_name_tool_calls`), the snapshots in
+`.../src/translate/snapshots/`, and `.../tests/live.rs`.
+
+## Intent
+
+`items_to_contents` makes one Gemini content for each core `Item`. Two defects follow.
+
+1. **Adjacent same-role contents.** A tool result becomes a `role: user` content with a
+   `functionResponse` part. When a user message comes directly after it, the request has two
+   adjacent `role: user` contents. Known sources of this shape:
+   - a turn-boundary checkpoint that returns `Inject(..)` after a tool turn (PR #346);
+   - a resumed run after a deferred tool call;
+   - a synthetic cancel result followed by the input of the next run;
+   - the handoff transcript note after a user message, when the transfer turn had no text
+     (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/loop_state.rs:770-789`);
+   - the `CompactingSession` prompt after a snapshot that ends in a tool result.
+   Parallel calls also give adjacent `model` contents (one per `ToolCall`) and adjacent `user`
+   contents (one per result).
+2. **Wrong name on a repeated call id.** The translator resolves a `functionResponse` name from one
+   global `call_id -> name` map, and the last call wins. `stream.rs` makes the fallback ids
+   `fc_{n}` per stream, so two turns can both have a call `fc_0`. Then an earlier result gets the
+   name of a later call (turn 1 `search`/`fc_0`, turn 2 `pay`/`fc_0` → the `search` result is sent
+   as `pay`).
+
+## Goals
+
+- The translator never sends two adjacent contents with the same role. It merges them into one
+  content and keeps the order of the parts.
+- The rule applies to every item, so replayed session items are also covered.
+- Each `functionResponse` gets the name of the call that it closes, by the core pairing rule
+  (below), within the limits in "Known limits".
+
+## Non-goals
+
+- Gemini thought signatures and `ContentPart::Reasoning` translation (still deferred, D3).
+- Changes to the fallback id scheme in `stream.rs`. A unique fallback id would remove the collision
+  for new histories, but stored sessions already hold repeated `fc_0` ids, so the translator must
+  pair by order anyway. A follow-up Linear issue can track the id scheme.
+- Changes to other providers.
+
+## Approaches
+
+1. **Merge after translation (picked).** Translate each item to `(role, parts)` as today, then fold
+   adjacent entries with the same role into one content. One small post-pass covers every source
+   of adjacency with one rule.
+2. **Merge at each push site.** Each branch checks the last content and appends to it. This repeats
+   the same check in five branches, and a new branch can forget it.
+3. **Reorder items in core before the provider sees them.** Rejected: the problem is a Gemini wire
+   rule, and other providers accept the core order as it is.
+
+Sven approved approach 1 on 2026-11-20, and approved this spec at GATE 1 on 2026-11-20.
+
+## Design
+
+### Merge
+
+- Build a `Vec<(role, Vec<Value>)>` in item order, then fold it: when the role of an entry equals
+  the role of the last merged entry, append its parts; else start a new content.
+- **Exception, the tool-result boundary** (added 2026-11-20 after the live run, Sven's decision):
+  a `user` entry whose first part is not a `functionResponse` does not merge into a `user` content
+  whose last part is a `functionResponse`. It starts a new `user` content. So a user text after a
+  tool result stays a separate content, as on `main`.
+  - Reason: Gemini 3 checks thought signatures only in the current turn, and the current turn
+    starts at the last `user` content that is not a tool result. With the merge, `user[fr, text]`
+    keeps the call in the current turn, and the translator sends no signature (SMA-827): HTTP 400
+    (probe shape 3 with no signature; the first live run of this branch failed 3 of 3 this way).
+    The split shape gets HTTP 200 with and without a signature (probe shape 2).
+  - Consequence: the SMA-804 `Inject` shape stays two adjacent `user` contents. The probe shows
+    that Gemini accepts it. Parallel results, adjacent user texts, and all `model` contents still
+    merge. Review this exception when SMA-827 lands.
+- An entry with no parts is dropped before the fold. Today only an empty `user` content is
+  dropped. An assistant message with only `Reasoning` parts gives a `model` content with
+  `"parts": []`.
+- An empty `ContentPart::Text` (`text == ""`) in a user or assistant message is dropped (SMA-804
+  spec §5.3 asks every translator to do this; SMA-819 did it for Anthropic). Without this, the
+  merge puts `{"text": ""}` into the content with the `functionResponse`.
+- `Item::System` stays in `systemInstruction` and does not take part in the merge. Items that the
+  translator skips, and `System` items, do not break adjacency.
+- Intended consequences:
+  - Parallel calls: N adjacent `ToolCall` items become one `model` content with N `functionCall`
+    parts, and N results become one `user` content with N `functionResponse` parts.
+  - An assistant text followed by its `ToolCall` becomes one `model` content (text part, then
+    `functionCall` part).
+  - Two adjacent user texts become two `text` parts in one content. They are not joined.
+- The order of parallel `functionCall` parts is the core item order. `build_items` in core emits
+  calls in `BTreeMap<call_id, _>` order (`crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/model.rs:514,530`), so
+  `fc_10` comes before `fc_2`. This spec does not change that. Note for D3: Gemini 3 puts the
+  thought signature on the first `functionCall` part.
+- The empty-conversation error stays: if no content remains after the fold, return the error.
+
+### Name resolution (core pairing rule, FIFO)
+
+- One pass in item order. The pass keeps a list of open calls (call id, name), in order. The
+  translator must not store names by call id in a pre-pass, because that brings the defect back.
+  The open-call state goes `&mut` into `user_parts`, or the pass stores names by occurrence.
+  - A `ToolCall` item, or a `ContentPart::ToolUse` in an `AssistantMessage`, adds an open call.
+  - A result (`Item::ToolResult`, or `ContentPart::ToolResult` in a `UserMessage`) closes the
+    **earliest** open call with its id and takes that name.
+- This is the rule that core uses: `resume_exec::paired_result` (`resume_exec.rs:200-220`, "each
+  result closes the earliest open call with its call id", "as in the session recorder") and
+  `deferral::agent_view` (`deferral.rs:585-620`). `run_tools_concurrent` returns one outcome per
+  call in call order (`agent.rs:748`). With FIFO, two calls in one round that share `fc_0` get the
+  correct names. The cross-turn `search`/`pay` case also works.
+  - **This changes the ticket text.** The ticket says "the most recent earlier call with the same
+    id that has no result yet" (LIFO). LIFO gives both names wrong for two same-id calls in one
+    round, where `main` gives one of two. Sven chose FIFO at GATE 1 on 2026-11-20.
+- A result that closes no open call, but that has an earlier call with its id (a second result for
+  one call), is **dropped** with a `tracing::warn!` (target `paigasus::gemini::translate`). This
+  matches `agent_view`, which drops a result that closes no open call. It also prevents a merged
+  `user` content with more `functionResponse` parts than its `functionCall` parts. (This replaces
+  the earlier call "use the most recent earlier call", which could send two responses for one
+  call.)
+- A result whose id has no earlier call returns an error:
+  - if a later item has a call with that id: a new message, `tool result for call_id {id} comes
+    before its call`;
+  - else the existing `tool result references unknown call_id {id}`.
+- Behavior change: a result before its call now gives an error. Today the global map accepts it.
+  No core producer makes this order: `close_open_transfers` inserts at `at + 1`
+  (`resume_exec.rs:194`), the resume block follows the calls of the earlier run, and the legacy
+  repair moves results after their calls. A stored session in this order now fails at `invoke`
+  instead of being sent. The commit message names this error so that the CHANGELOG shows it.
+
+### Invariant and known limits
+
+The merge depends on one invariant: the next `user` content answers each `functionCall` of a
+`model` content. Two real core histories do not hold it:
+
+1. **Open deferred calls.** `RunDeferred` leaves calls with no result. `CompactingSession` sends
+   `snapshot + prompt` to its model (`compacting_session.rs:200-211`). With a Gemini summarizer
+   this gives, for example, `model[fc c1, fc c2], user[fr c1, text]`. Probe shape 14 shows what
+   Gemini does with it. This spec does not add synthetic results; if shape 14 fails, a follow-up
+   issue covers it.
+2. **Replay of a `ParallelAgent` session.** Sibling events interleave through `select_all`
+   (`workflow.rs:377`), and sibling Gemini agents all start at `fc_0`. The merge can put two
+   `functionCall` parts with the same id into one content. No order rule can name those results
+   correctly. This spec does not fix it.
+
+## Tests
+
+Unit tests in `request.rs` assert the full `contents` array, as
+`tool_result_then_user_message_request_shape` does:
+
+- `tool_result_then_user_message_request_shape` (and its doc comment): the assistant text and
+  the call merge into one `model` content; the `functionResponse` content and the user text stay
+  two `user` contents (the tool-result boundary). The ticket asked for one merged `user` content;
+  Sven changed that on 2026-11-20 after the live run.
+- The tool-result boundary: a user text after results stays separate; a result after a result
+  still merges; a user text after a user text still merges.
+- More than two adjacent contents with the same role merge into one, in order (a result, then two
+  user messages).
+- Two calls in different turns that share `fc_0` (`search`, then `pay`): correct name on each
+  `functionResponse`.
+- Two calls in one round that share `fc_0` (`search`, then `pay`), as two `ToolCall` items and as
+  two `ToolUse` parts in one `AssistantMessage`: the first result is `search`, the second `pay`.
+- Results in a different order than the calls (distinct ids): each gets its own name.
+- A second result for one call is dropped.
+- A result before its call gives the new error.
+- A nested `ContentPart::ToolResult` mixed with `Text` in a `UserMessage`, directly after an
+  `Item::ToolResult`: one merged `user` content with correct names.
+- An `Item::System` between two user messages: one merged `user` content.
+- A reasoning-only assistant message is dropped and its neighbours merge.
+- An empty `Text` part is dropped.
+
+Snapshots: update `snap_parallel_same_name_tool_calls` and its inline asserts in `mod.rs`, and any
+other snapshot that the merge changes. Review each snapshot diff by hand.
+
+Live test (mandatory, `#[ignore]` in `tests/live.rs`, needs `GEMINI_API_KEY`): call
+`GeminiModel::invoke` with `search` and `pay` declared, for three histories: the SMA-804 shape
+(result then user text), one parallel round, and a cross-turn `fc_0` collision. Assert no `Err`
+event and a `Finish` event. This is the "after" check through the real translator.
+
+## Live check (acceptance criterion)
+
+The probe `probe.sh` sends hand-made request bodies to `gemini-2.5-flash` through the REST API
+(`generateContent`), with `search` and `pay` declared. It prints the HTTP status, the finish reason
+and a short part summary. It never prints request headers. The probe source goes into the commit
+body. Shapes:
+
+1. baseline: `user, model[fc], user[fr]`
+2. SMA-804 today: `..., user[fr], user[text]`
+3. SMA-804 merged: `..., user[fr, text]`
+4. three adjacent `user` contents
+5. parallel today: `model[fc0], model[fc1], user[fr0], user[fr1]`
+6. parallel merged: `model[fc0, fc1], user[fr0, fr1]`
+7. `functionResponse` name differs from its `functionCall` name
+8. repeated `fc_0` across turns, correct names
+9. repeated `fc_0` across turns, today's wrong name
+10. `model[text, fc]`
+11. parallel merged, responses in a different order than the calls
+12. `user[fr, {"text": ""}]`
+13. two `functionResponse` parts for one call
+14. parallel merged, one call has no response, then text
+
+Pass rule for a target shape (3, 6, 8, 10, 11): HTTP 200, `finishReason: STOP`, and an answer that
+uses the tool result.
+
+Order: run the probe **before** any code. If Gemini rejects shape 3 or 6, stop and bring it back to
+Sven before implementation (fallback: keep the merge for `model` contents only, or put the text in a
+separate content after a synthetic `model` turn; Sven decides).
+
+### Results before the fix (2026-11-20, Developer API, hand-made bodies)
+
+`gemini-2.5-flash` and `gemini-2.5-flash-lite`: HTTP 404 on every shape, "no longer available to
+new users". The probe therefore ran on `gemini-3.8-flash`.
+
+`gemini-3.8-flash` with no `thoughtSignature`: HTTP 400 "Function call is missing a
+thought_signature in functionCall parts" on every shape in which the call is in the current turn
+(1, 3, 5-14). Shapes 2 and 4 returned HTTP 200 / `STOP`, because the trailing user text moves the
+call into an earlier turn, and Gemini checks signatures only in the current turn.
+
+`gemini-3.8-flash` with the documented dummy signature `skip_thought_signature_validator` on each
+`functionCall` part:
+
+| Shape | Result |
+|---|---|
+| 1 baseline | 200 STOP, uses the result |
+| 2 SMA-804 today (two adjacent `user`) | 200 STOP, uses the result |
+| 3 SMA-804 merged | 200 STOP, uses the result |
+| 4 three adjacent `user` | 200 STOP |
+| 5 parallel today | 200 STOP |
+| 6 parallel merged | 200 STOP |
+| 7 response name differs from call name | **400 "Request contains an invalid argument."** |
+| 8 repeated `fc_0`, correct names | 200 STOP |
+| 9 repeated `fc_0`, today's wrong name | **400 "Request contains an invalid argument."** |
+| 10 `model[text, fc]` | 200 STOP |
+| 11 merged, responses reordered | 200 STOP |
+| 12 `user[fr, {"text": ""}]` | 200 STOP |
+| 13 two responses for one call | 200 STOP |
+| 14 merged, one call with no response | 200 STOP, the model calls `search` again |
+
+What this means:
+
+- Defect 1 (adjacent same-role contents) causes no failure on `gemini-3.8-flash`. With a signature,
+  both the split and the merged shapes are accepted. Without a signature, only the split shape is
+  accepted (shapes 2 vs 3). So the merge keeps the tool-result boundary (see "Merge").
+- Defect 2 (wrong name) is a **hard failure**: HTTP 400 on the next model call. Part 2 is the fix
+  that matters for users.
+- Gemini accepts a second response for one call (13). The translator still drops it, to match core.
+- Shape 14 (an open call with no response) is accepted. Known limit 1 causes no API error.
+
+### Out of scope, found by the probe
+
+The Gemini provider does not read or send `thoughtSignature` (no match in `crates/`). With a
+current Gemini model, every request in which the current turn holds a `functionCall` gets HTTP 400.
+So tool loops on Gemini 3.x fail at the second model call. SMA-827 tracks this. The model ids in
+the crate docs and in `tests/live.rs` (`gemini-2.5-flash`) are not available to new users; SMA-565
+tracks them. This PR changes only the `tests/live.rs` default (below); the other occurrences stay
+in SMA-565.
+
+### After the fix
+
+The live test in `tests/live.rs` runs through the real translator. Because the translator sends no
+thought signatures, each history in the test ends with a user text after the last tool result. With
+the tool-result boundary, that text is a separate `user` content, so no call is in the current turn.
+(The first version of this section assumed this without the boundary. The first live run proved it
+wrong: 3 of 3 tests got HTTP 400 for a missing thought signature.) Shape 9 shows that Gemini checks names in earlier turns too, so the
+cross-turn `fc_0` history still tests the name fix. The test model defaults to `gemini-3.8-flash`
+(override with `GEMINI_MODEL_ID`); the default of the existing `dev_model()` changes from
+`gemini-2.5-flash` to `gemini-3.8-flash`, because the old default returns 404 for new users.
+
+Results after the fix (2026-11-20, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini
+--test live -- --ignored live_developer_`):
+
+| Live test | This branch | Control: same test file on `main` (e7ac5377) |
+|---|---|---|
+| `live_developer_text_turn` | pass | pass |
+| `live_developer_structured_output` | pass | pass |
+| `live_developer_tool_result_then_user_text` | pass | pass |
+| `live_developer_parallel_round` | pass | pass |
+| `live_developer_cross_turn_repeated_call_id` | pass | **fail: HTTP 400 "Request contains an invalid argument."** |
+
+The first run of this branch, before the tool-result boundary, failed the three tool tests with
+HTTP 400 "Function call is missing a thought_signature".
+
+Scope of the check: Developer API only. Vertex uses the same translator.
+
+## Docs and release
+
+- No book or README page describes the old shape, so no book or README edit is needed.
+- release-plz bumps `paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini` (patch) and the facade by cascade. No hand
+  version bump.
+
+## Left to the builder
+
+- Helper names, and how the open-call state reaches `user_parts`, within the one-pass rule above.

--- 973790aa test(providers): SMA-820 add live tests for tool results and repeated call ids
Three ignored live tests send tool histories through GeminiModel::invoke.
Each history ends with a user text, because the translator sends no thought
signatures yet (SMA-827). The dev_model() default changes to gemini-3.8-flash,
because gemini-2.5-flash returns 404 for new users.

On gemini-3.8-flash all five live tests pass. The same test file on main fails
live_developer_cross_turn_repeated_call_id with HTTP 400.

Probe used for the before check (hand-made REST bodies, results in the spec):

    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    # SMA-820 live probe: how does the Gemini API handle each contents shape?
    # Needs GEMINI_API_KEY in the environment. Never prints the key.
    set -u
    MODEL="${1:-gemini-2.5-flash}"
    URL="https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/${MODEL}:generateContent"
    TOOLS='[{"functionDeclarations":[
      {"name":"search","description":"Search the web","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"q":{"type":"string"}}}},
      {"name":"pay","description":"Pay a bill","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"amount":{"type":"number"}}}}]}]'

    U()   { printf '{"role":"user","parts":[{"text":"%s"}]}' "$1"; }
    FC()  { if [ -n "${SIG:-}" ]; then printf '{"functionCall":{"id":"%s","name":"%s","args":%s},"thoughtSignature":"%s"}' "$1" "$2" "$3" "$SIG"; else printf '{"functionCall":{"id":"%s","name":"%s","args":%s}}' "$1" "$2" "$3"; fi; }
    FR()  { printf '{"functionResponse":{"id":"%s","name":"%s","response":%s}}' "$1" "$2" "$3"; }

# release-plz.toml — automated versioning, changelogs, GitHub releases.
# Reference: https://release-plz.dev/docs/config

[workspace]
# Bump dependent crates whenever a dep's version changes. The facade
# (paigasus-helikon) depends on every sibling via `[workspace.dependencies]`,
# so a `feat(core):` commit triggers: paigasus-helikon-core bumped →
# facade's `[workspace.dependencies].paigasus-helikon-core` line updated →
# facade itself gets a patch bump.
dependencies_update = true

# Force the scopeless release-PR title + commit (`chore: release`). release-plz's
# default SINGLE-crate template is `chore({package}): release {version}`, which uses
# the full package name (e.g. `paigasus-helikon`) as the Conventional-Commits scope —
# not in the convco/.versionrc + pr-title.yml allowlist (which uses short scopes like
# `facade`), so both the `commits` and `pr-title` gates reject it. The scopeless form
# matches the historical multi-crate release PRs and passes both. (Diagnosed on PR #58,
# the first facade-only release.)
pr_name = "chore: release"

# All library crates publish to crates.io (Stage 1 SMA-385 onward; the last
# stubs ascended in SMA-332/SMA-333). Remaining per-package overrides below
# are the only exceptions. See CLAUDE.md for the 4-step recipe a stub
# follows when it ascends.

[changelog]
sort_commits = "newest"

# Internal test harnesses: these three workspace members never publish.
# publish = false in each Cargo.toml and release = false here MUST move
# together.

# Internal cross-runtime HTTP wire-format conformance suite: boots BOTH the axum

publish = false
release = false

# published, so it carries the same publish=false / release=false pair as the

## Limitations

The following content types are silently dropped during request translation:

- **Remote-URL images** — only inline base64-encoded images are forwarded; `ContentPart::ImageUrl` variants with remote URLs are omitted.
- **Audio parts** — audio `ContentPart` variants are not supported by this provider and are dropped.
- **Non-text tool-result parts** — only the text content of tool results is forwarded; image or structured-data parts in tool results are omitted.

The following feature is not yet implemented:

- **Reasoning streaming** — Gemini's `thoughtsContent` field in streaming responses is currently discarded. Reasoning delta events (`ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta`) are not emitted by this provider. This will be addressed in a future release.

## Limitations

The following content types are silently dropped during request translation:

- **Remote-URL images** — only inline base64-encoded images are forwarded; `ContentPart::ImageUrl` variants with remote URLs are omitted.
- **Audio parts** — audio `ContentPart` variants are not supported by this provider and are dropped.
- **Non-text tool-result parts** — only the text content of tool results is forwarded; image or structured-data parts in tool results are omitted.

The following feature is not yet implemented:

- **Reasoning streaming** — Gemini's `thoughtsContent` field in streaming responses is currently discarded. Reasoning delta events (`ModelEvent::ReasoningDelta`) are not emitted by this provider. This will be addressed in a future release.

## SMA-820 whole-branch review (e7ac5377..973790aa)

I found no Critical issues. The code change is correct and matches the core FIFO rule. Two Important items are about the release record and ticket tracking, not the code. Some Minor items are text that is now wrong in docs and comments.

### Strengths
- **`OpenCalls` is correct.**
  - It does one pass in item order. It opens calls from `Item::ToolCall` and from `ContentPart::ToolUse`, in part order.
  - It closes the earliest open call with the same id. This is the same rule as `resume_exec::paired_result` (resume_exec.rs:200-220) and `deferral::agent_view` (deferral.rs:605-618). `agent_view` also drops a result that closes no open call, so the duplicate drop matches core.
  - The `all` set only selects the error message. It stores no names by id, so the old defect cannot come back.
  - The lifetimes are sound.
- **`merge_same_role` is small and keeps the part order.** It drops empty entries before the fold, so `"parts": []` cannot occur. The empty-conversation check runs after the merge.
- **The tests assert full `contents` arrays.** They cover each Review Focus item: duplicate as the only part, `user("")` only, same-id `ToolUse` parts, text + `ToolUse` + `ToolCall`, and `System` between user messages.
- **The live evidence is a real A/B.** The same test file passes 5/5 on the branch and fails `live_developer_cross_turn_repeated_call_id` with HTTP 400 on main. The probe source is in the body of commit 973790aa, as the spec requires.
- **Gates I ran on the branch all pass:**
  - `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini --all-features`
  - `cargo test` on `paigasus-helikon-provider-stream-conformance` and `paigasus-helikon-workspace-lints` (tracing-target coverage)
  - `cargo clippy -p paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini --all-features --all-targets -D warnings`
  - rustdoc `-D warnings` for the crate
  - `cargo fmt --check`
  - markdownlint on the two new `.md` files: 0 issues. `docs/superpowers/**` is also excluded in `.markdownlint-cli2.jsonc`.
- **Commit rules are met.** The scopes `providers`, `specs` and `plan` are in the `.versionrc` `scopeRegex`. No `Cargo.toml` changed, so there is no hand version bump.

### Issues

**Critical:** none.

**Important (should fix)**

1. **The CHANGELOG will not show the new error.**
   - What: the spec says "The commit message names this error so that the CHANGELOG shows it." Only the body of 30e3a1ea names it.
   - Why: `main-protection-reviews.json` allows only squash merges. The release-plz changelog template uses only the subject line of each commit on `main`, which here is the PR title. So the new `tool result for call_id {id} comes before its call` error, and the drop of duplicate results, are not visible to users. The error is a behavior change: main accepted these histories.
   - How: put the behavior change in the PR title, or edit the CHANGELOG entry in the release-plz `chore: release` PR by hand. In both cases also state it in the PR body.

2. **SMA-820 closes, but its headline shape still ships.**
   - What: the tool-result boundary keeps `user[fr], user[text]` as two adjacent `user` contents. This is the SMA-804 `Inject` shape, which is the ticket title. The owner chose this on purpose, and the probe shows Gemini accepts it.
   - Why: Linear auto-closes SMA-820 when the PR merges. The spec says "Review this exception when SMA-827 lands", but no ticket tracks that review.
   - How: add that note to SMA-827 in Linear, or file a follow-up issue. State the remaining shape in the PR body.

**Minor (nice to have)**

3. **Spec text that the boundary decision made false** (docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-sma-820-gemini-merge-same-role-contents-design.md):
   - The Goals section still says "The translator never sends two adjacent contents with the same role."
   - The Tests section still says "More than two adjacent contents with the same role merge into one, in order (a result, then two user messages)." The real test `adjacent_user_texts_merge_but_not_into_a_tool_result` asserts two `user` contents.
   - How: update both lines.
   - Also, Known limit 1 says that `CompactingSession` sends open deferred calls. But `maybe_compact` skips compaction when a deferral is open (crates/paigasus-helikon-core/src/compacting_session.rs:171-179). That path cannot occur. Only the `ParallelAgent` sibling case is real.

4. **The plan was not updated after the owner's ruling** (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-11-20-sma-820-gemini-merge-same-role-contents.md, Task 2):
   - It still expects `user[fr, text]` for `tool_result_then_user_message_request_shape`.
   - It still names a test `more_than_two_adjacent_same_role_contents_merge_in_order` that does not exist.
   - How: add one note that points to the boundary ruling.

5. **A wrong comment** (crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/src/translate/request.rs:201).
   - The comment says "Gemini rejects an empty text part." Probe shape 12 (`user[fr, {"text": ""}]`) got 200 STOP on the Developer API.
   - How: change the comment to cite SMA-804 §5.3 ("every translator drops empty text") instead of a Gemini rejection.

6. **A vague doc comment on `merge_same_role`** (request.rs, around lines 255-261). This was parked in the ledger.
   - The text "a merged text makes it see the call there" does not explain the rule.
   - How: write that Gemini starts the current turn at the last `user` content that is not a tool result, and that a text joined to a result keeps the unsigned `functionCall` in that turn (HTTP 400).

7. **The boundary only applies in one direction.**
   - What: a `user` entry that starts with a `functionResponse` still merges into a `user` content that ends in text. `model[fc], user[text], user[fr]` becomes `user[text, fr]`.
   - On main this was split, so the text started a new turn and the call was in an earlier turn. Merged, it can put the unsigned call back in the current turn. This is the same failure that the boundary prevents.
   - I found no core producer that puts a user text between a call and its result, so the risk is low. No test covers it.
   - How: make the rule symmetric (do not merge when exactly one side is a `functionResponse`) and add one test. Or record it as a known limit.

8. **The crate README does not list the new drops** (crates/paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini/README.md, "Limitations").
   - The section lists what translation silently drops. The translator now also drops a second tool result for one call (with a warning) and empty text parts.
   - How: add one bullet. The book needs no edit. `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md` does not describe the wire shape, and the `translate` target is already in observability-evaluation.md:127.

9. **No test merges three or more contents of one role.** All the merge tests merge two. Add one test with three parallel results.

### Parked findings triage
- **T1, no test for the warn output:** fine to leave. The drop itself has tests (`duplicate_result_*`), and the target string is the existing `paigasus::gemini::translate`.
- **T1, doc reflow:** fine to leave. It is cosmetic, and fmt and rustdoc pass.
- **T1, nested "before its call" path not tested:** fine to leave. The nested `ContentPart::ToolResult` path and the top-level path call the same `close()`.
- **T2, no assistant empty-Text test:** already fixed. `empty_text_in_assistant_message_is_dropped` is in 6c4a1bed.
- **T2, mid-message empty text:** fine to leave. It is the same `filter` arm as the tested case.
- **T2, `INSTA_UPDATE=always`:** fine to leave. Only the expected snapshot changed, and no `.snap.new` files remain.
- **T2 fix round, vague doc comment:** fix before merge. It is cheap, and it is the only record in the code of why the boundary exists (item 6).
- **T2 fix round, two boundary edges not tested:** the "fr after fr, then text" edge is covered by `nested_result_and_text_merge_with_preceding_tool_result`. The "fr after text" edge is item 7. Fix it, or record it as a known limit.
- **T3, overlong spec line:** fine to leave. markdownlint reports 0 issues, and `docs/superpowers/**` is excluded from the CI lint.

### Declined to judge
- **Vertex path:** I did not judge it. There is no live run, and the spec limits the check to the Developer API.
- **`ParallelAgent` replay with sibling ids that collide:** this is a known limit in the spec, and no order rule can fix it.
- **The core legacy transfer repair uses LIFO for non-transfer calls** (session.rs:530-533, `rposition`), but the translator uses FIFO. I did not judge this:
  - It is core code that this branch does not change.
  - The two rules give different results only when two calls with the same id are open at the same time, which `stream.rs` fallback ids prevent within one stream.
- **A result before its call when an earlier call with the same id is already closed:** this is dropped as a duplicate, not reported as an error. No core producer makes this order, so I did not judge it.
- **Did main's `user[fr1, text]` pass on Gemini 3?** I could not check this without a probe. It does not affect my findings, because the branch gives the same result under either turn rule that Gemini could use.

### Assessment
Ready to merge: **With fixes.** The translator change is correct, it matches core, and the live A/B proves it. Before merge, make the new error visible in the squashed PR title or the release CHANGELOG (item 1), and track the boundary review on SMA-827 (item 2). The spec, plan and comment corrections (items 3-6) are cheap, and I recommend them in the same PR.
